record.context_brief: FOL with modulo counting on tournaments
record.original_question: More generally, can one represent a total order on the vertices of an arbitrary tournament by first coloring the vertices and then using a first-order formula with modulo-counting predicates to define the relation x < y? That is, does there exist such a definability scheme for all tournaments in FOL plus modulo counting?

evidence.quote: There exists c, and φ logical formula, such that for all tournament T there exists a total order on the vertices, a coloring λ such that x < y iff T,λ satifies φ(x, y).
In general, with FOL + modulo counting ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let FO+MOD denote first-order logic on relational structures augmented with modulo-counting quantifiers (i.e., for each integer m≥2 and each residue r∈{0,…,m−1}, a quantifier ∃^{r mod m} x. ψ(x) asserting that the number of elements x satisfying ψ is congruent to r modulo m).

A tournament is a finite directed graph T=(V,E) such that for every pair of distinct vertices u,v∈V, exactly one of (u,v),(v,u) belongs to E. A vertex coloring of T with k colors is a map λ:V→{1,…,k}, regarded as a unary-predicate expansion (T,λ) of T.

Question. Does there exist an integer k≥1 and an FO+MOD formula φ(x,y) in the vocabulary consisting of the binary edge relation of tournaments together with k unary predicates (representing the colors), such that for every tournament T=(V,E) there exists a coloring λ:V→{1,…,k} and a total (linear) order < on V with the property that, for all u,v∈V,
   u < v   ⇔   (T,λ) ⊨ φ(u,v)?

Equivalently: can a linear order on the vertices of every tournament be defined by a fixed FO+MOD formula after a suitable bounded coloring of the vertices?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface a direct resolution of whether a fixed FO+MOD formula together with a bounded vertex coloring can define a linear order on every tournament. Related work studies FO+MOD transductions on bounded-expansion classes (where FO+MOD collapses to existential FO after a monadic expansion), and first-order definable colorings, but tournaments form a dense class outside that scope and the specific definability scheme asked here does not appear to be settled in the located sources.

status_evidence.title: Modulo-Counting First-Order Logic on Bounded Expansion Classes
status_evidence.snippet: On bounded expansion classes, every FO+MOD formula is equivalent, after a monadic expansion, to an existential FO formula; whether FO+MOD transductions are strictly more powerful than FO transductions in general is not clear.
status_evidence.claim: The general expressive power of FO+MOD transductions versus FO transductions, including on tournament-like dense classes, is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: On First-Order Definable Colorings
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which colorings/relations on classes of structures are first-order definable; does not address linear-order definability on all tournaments via FO+MOD with bounded coloring.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related definability questions are studied, but the tournament/FO+MOD ordering question is not addressed.
